reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

A U.N. human rights panel has now, for a second time, found that Israel is committing genocidal acts in Gaza, this time doing so specifically since the “ceasefire” has been in place. They also say that Israel is committing crimes against humanity in the West Bank.

When we have a conclusive body of evidence in front of us, as we do here, I feel that I, as an elected official, have a moral responsibility to speak out. If our government still will not do so as a whole, that responsibility is even more important. This is why I originally did so in September 2025 and why so many Americans have come to the same conclusion on their own.

My grandfather was murdered on a death march from Mauthausen concentration camp in the last few weeks of World War II – my family knows the impact antisemitism can have when left unchecked firsthand. We must continue to stand up with a clear voice against the frightening rise of antisemitism we’re seeing at home and around the globe. We must speak out against antisemitism and hold Israel accountable for its actions. We can do both. We must do both.

I want both a safe and secure Israel and a safe, secure independent Palestinian state. The fact is that the actions of the current Israeli government are not only not keeping people safe but are instead further isolating Israel on the world stage. In this moment, speaking truth and demanding change are the first steps on the path forward.

These powerful testimonials will be front of mind for me when I head back to D.C. https://t.co/B9ui7Q9ACv

So many families in Vermont and across our country know someone who has had breast cancer. That’s why it’s so important that we recognize National Mammography Day. 
 
Early detection of breast cancer is critical and can save your life. Call your doctor and set up a mammogram today.

The violence we’re seeing toward Palestinian civilians and members of the press in Israeli settlements is unacceptable. As is the Israeli government's enabling of it.
 
That's why I'm an original cosponsor of the Stop the Settlements Act which would sanction settlers to stop the construction of new settlements and expansion of existing ones. This is essential to stop the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians and create a true pathway to peace.

I just completed my unannounced oversight visit to the ICE facility in Burlington, MA, where many VT detainees are taken. 

I was especially focused on the conditions women are facing here and deeply upset at what I saw. We must keep the pressure on and call out this inhumanity. https://t.co/qiBuiEV26p

I’ll be checking back in soon. https://t.co/BX2C4LHaFg

As a former teacher and a parent, I’m absolutely heartsick. For these young children and this teacher who were so senselessly taken from their loved ones, and for this whole community who will now be forced to contend with this tragedy.

I helped pass Vermont’s first gun safety laws, so I know it’s possible. We must come together and end this national cycle of violence and devastation.

Women20 (W20) is dedicated to shaping a future free of inequality and discrimination for women and girls across the countries in the G20. This week, they brought their summit to Vermont!
 
Yesterday, it was my honor to be at the Haskell Free Library and Opera House to deliver remarks and welcome the delegates to our state.
 
No matter where we are in the world, women and girls need to see that their work will be valued, that their families will be supported, that their voices will be heard, and that their children will have opportunities to build lives that are meaningful and secure. I’m committed to doing all I can to make that a reality worldwide.

I’m so grateful for the roundtable we hosted today in Brattleboro with leaders from both sides of the U.S.-Canada border.

🇺🇸🇨🇦 https://t.co/4ZSDCOZgAW

Earlier today, I was honored to host @RepMcGovern, Canadian Consul General @BernJordanCG, the Quebec Government Office’s Olivia Dion, and small businesses from both Vermont and Massachusetts in Brattleboro. We visited Allard Lumber in town and had a very important roundtable conversation about the U.S.-Canada relationship and the impacts of the trade war on folks on both sides of the border.
 
We heard repeatedly that businesses need stability. The constant and abrupt changes to our trade policy deprive businesses of the opportunity to plan ahead. It’s forcing them to take their attention away from serving their customers just to navigate all the red tape.
 
Nevertheless, the economic, community and personal ties between our two countries remain strong. Vermont and Canada have been interconnected for generations and we’re doing everything we can to keep it that way.

roll_calls.question: On Passage — Major Richard Star Act (H R 2102)
roll_calls.plain_language: Official question: On Passage. H.R. 2102: Major Richard Star Act. Result: Passed.

post.text:
We just passed the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act by a vote of 392-18! This bill will allow wounded veterans to keep more of their retirement and disability pay, and help more vets retire with dignity.
 
We have a sacred obligation to make sure veterans have the care they need when they come home, and this bill delivers on that obligation.

Republican leadership did all they could to stop this bill from coming to the floor, but we refused to give up. We'll never stop fighting for our vets.
